paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: Ablation studies between Consistency-Bi and Consistency-Uni on test set of IWSLT14 De-En task of wait-k policy.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the BLEU scores achieved by three different consistency-based methods—Consistency-CE, Consistency-Uni, and Consistency-Bi—as a function of Average Lagging (AL) on the test set of the IWSLT14 De-En task under the wait-k policy. The x-axis represents Average Lagging (AL), ranging from 1 to 9 with linear spacing and integer tick marks. The y-axis represents BLEU score, ranging from 20 to 32 with linear spacing and tick marks at every 2 units. The Consistency-CE method is shown as a purple dashed line with circular markers, starting at approximately 19.5 BLEU at AL=1 and increasing steadily to around 31.0 BLEU at AL=9. The Consistency-Uni method is represented by a green solid line with square markers, beginning at about 25.0 BLEU at AL=2 and rising to approximately 32.0 BLEU at AL=9. The Consistency-Bi method is depicted as a red solid line with star markers, starting at roughly 26.0 BLEU at AL=2 and increasing to about 32.0 BLEU at AL=9. All three lines show an upward trend with increasing AL, with Consistency-Uni and Consistency-Bi achieving higher BLEU scores than Consistency-CE across the range, and the two former methods showing similar performance at higher AL values.
